newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical intros new heart surgery tool.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical intros new heart surgery tool.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp said it introduced the first set of instruments for minimally invasive coronary bypass graft surgery, enabling surgeons operate on a heart through a three- to four-inch incision.
Normally, surgeons make a 12-inch incision to operate on the heart, the company said.
The new instruments also reduced operating time and stilled the heart, eliminating the need for a heart lung machine and avoiding the risk of blood damage, it said.
The entire set, apart from the clamp, had already been cleared for marketing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and would be launched in January, the company said.

The tools included a retractor base to keep the incision open during surgery, a site stabilizer to control the heart's movement, a clamp to stop the blood flow through the target artery and a so-called SurgiStich, to let surgeons sew vessels together in a confined space.

The company, which unveiled the product at the American College of Surgeons meeting in San Francisco, said it also introduced a new technology for treating benign prostate hyperplasia, or an enlargement of the prostate which constricted the urethra.

The condition affected more than 13 million men worldwide, it said. The company said its technology, which uses radio waves and a flexible scope, allowes surgeons to perform the procedure in their offices under local anesthesia.
Other products the company introduced include two laparoscopic tools - a stapling and cutting tool and an ultra-sonic shear, used to coagulate and divide tissue.

U.S. Surgical also said at the conference that it formed an exclusive worldwide marketing agreement with Vitex, which developed a fibrin glue product. So far, the product had not been approved in the United States, it said.
